rows: 8 sites with 31 alternatives, No Action included
Average annual habitat units (AAHU); lift is the output above No Action

Riparian, left bank: an index (0 to 1) times acres at each target year; Riparian, right bank: an index (0 to 1) times acres at each target year; Instream: an index (0 to 1) times acres at each target year
Straight lines between target years, averaged over the span of the years

Capital recovery factor times the first costs, interest during construction and the present value of OMRRR; interest during construction from even spending (middle of each period); OMRRR discounted from the end of each year
Cost rounded to 4 and output to 6 decimals before comparing
One alternative per site: each site's recommendation
P128 (National Ecosystem Restoration (NER) plan), to review after changes
Concrete channel removal with left bank wetland
Large wood structures for 50% of reach
The chain of wetlands gives the largest lift for a cost close to the other alternatives; it is the site's only best buy besides No Action.
Channel removal with a left bank wetland addresses the concrete channel directly, with a large lift and a low unit cost.
Channel and bank stabilization without beaver removal is the site's best buy and gives the most lift.
The largest best buy: the most lift in the watershed at the lowest unit cost.
The largest best buy, with a low unit cost like Site 2A.
No Action, needs review after changes
The unit costs of both best buys are far above every other site, so no action is recommended at this site.
The largest best buy, and a place to demonstrate innovative low-cost methods.
The largest best buy, with high lift for South Utoy Creek.
Cost-effective plan added: near parity between North and South Utoy, and it introduces the innovative actions at 3F.
Removed because P16 already introduces Site 3F.
Only one sub-watershed; the study's scope emphasized actions across the whole watershed.
Only North Utoy Creek; the first plan with actions in both sub-watersheds is P14.
The smallest acceptable plan: the first with actions in both the North and South Utoy sub-watersheds.
Site 3F adds high benefit at low cost and demonstrates innovative methods for the region.
Site 17B extends actions upstream and cuts sediment delivered to Sites 2A and 2B.
Site 17D2E begins to address the concrete channel, a major cause of degradation.
Site 17F2M addresses the largest extent of concrete channel; working with 17D2E should cut mobilization costs, and the plan has the widest coverage.
P128 (National Ecosystem Restoration (NER) plan), to review after changes

All seven sites: the widest geographic coverage, and it directly addresses the concrete channel that drives degradation in the watershed. Sites can still be dropped after further analysis such as real estate.
